source.extractionTool: pdftotext (poppler) -enc UTF-8 raw and -layout modes; pdfplumber for sub/superscript, glyph and drawn-arrow checks
source.usage: Official CISCE board examination paper from the CISCE Archive Library (cisce.org/archive-library); question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.
source.notes: No official marking scheme is published with this paper; questions carry no official answer. ICSE 2024 board examination paper, Chemistry (Science Paper – 2), from the official CISCE Archive Library ZIP bundle ICSE_2024_QP.zip; every page footer prints 'T24 522' (used as paperCode); the year 2024 comes from the bundle/file name and the 'T24' prefix. Maximum Marks 80, Time allowed Two hours, 12 printed pages. Section A (Questions 1–2, 40 marks) is compulsory; Section B (Questions 3–8, 10 marks each) says 'Attempt any four questions', so the printed marks in this pack add up to 100 (40 + 6 × 10), which is expected. Question 1 (i)–(xv) are 1-mark MCQs (the [15] is the Question 1 total). Where a printed mark covers several lettered sub-parts, each sub-part is its own entry with the mark split evenly (marksSource SECTION_INSTRUCTIONS) and the shared instruction/stem repeated in its text. Chemical formula subscripts and ionic charges are printed as smaller lowered/raised glyphs and were rebuilt as Unicode (H₂SO₄, Pb²⁺, 10²³) after checking glyph size and baseline with pdfplumber; most reaction arrows are an unmapped Wingdings glyph (U+F0E0) rendered as →; two arrows in Q4(iii)(b)-(c) are drawn lines with conditions (∆, CaO) printed above/below; the reversible arrows in Q6(i) extract as ⇋ (U+21CB). Tables (Q3(iv), Q7(iv)) and matching columns (Q2(ii), Q8(iii)) are flattened into text. Figures not reproduced: the electroplating sketch (page 5, Q2(i)) and the two structural formulae for IUPAC naming (page 6, Q2(v)(a)).

What is the property of sulphuric acid that makes it a suitable reagent for the reaction?
